text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Israeli newspapers on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
JERUSALEM POST
- Defence Minister Mordechai leads budget protest.
- Ten tourists hurt in attack in Jaffa.
- Brussels meeting between Palestinian President Arafat and Israeli Foreign Minister Levy 'positive'.
- Beirut building boom only a facelift.
- Bezeq Telcom workers return to work this morning.
- Report on bridge that plunged into river with Jewish athletes due today.
- Pro-Israeli South Lebanese Army commander Lahd considers withdrawal from Jezzine south Lebanon enclave - Lebanese newspapers.
- Tower Semiconductor Ltd mulls $1.25 billion overseas plant.
- Industrial production rises more than five percent in April-May.
HAARETZ
- Levy, Arafat agree to begin negotiations on "safe passage" and Gaza port.
- Israeli Arab runs down group of tourists and stabs two in Jaffa; police think incident terror attack.
- Estimate: Those responsible for collapse of bridge are engineers and contractors.
- Workers sanctions expected tomorrow at Ben-Gurion International Airport, by electric company workers, and in health clinics in solidarity with Bezeq workers.
- Mordechai boycotts cabinet meeting to protest planned budget cut.
- Charles Bronfman appointed chairman of Koor; Kobler to replace Gaon.
- Managing director of Pelephone dismissed by Motorola.
MAARIV
- Revelation: new witness says: I checked the computer and warned that the bridge would collapse.
- In Brussels a good meeting between Arafat and Levy.
- Apparent terror attack in Jaffa.
YEDIOTH AHRONOTH
- Arab runs down and stabs 11 tourists.
- Bezeq work disruptions today also.
- Arafat to Levy: No chance that I will give up on the second Israeli West Bank pullback.
